PCI.grpDescription: Set of tools for PCI / PCIe troubleshooting

PCIDeviceList.title: PCI Device List
PCIDeviceList.description: Every device on the PCI/PCIe bus, with numeric vendor:device IDs. No output at all means nothing enumerated - check that the slot is enabled in config.txt and that the link trained (see PCI Kernel Messages).
PCIDeviceList.cmd: if [ ! -d /sys/bus/pci/devices ]; then echo "No PCI bus present on this system"; elif ! command -v lspci >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "lspci not installed (pciutils package)"; else lspci -nn; fi

PCIDeviceTree.title: PCI Device Tree
PCIDeviceTree.description: PCI bus topology. Devices sitting behind a PCIe switch or bridge (multi-port adapter cards) appear indented underneath it.
PCIDeviceTree.cmd: if [ ! -d /sys/bus/pci/devices ]; then echo "No PCI bus present on this system"; elif ! command -v lspci >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "lspci not installed (pciutils package)"; else lspci -tvnn; fi

PCIDrivers.title: PCI Drivers and Link Status
PCIDrivers.description: Which kernel driver claimed each PCI device, plus the negotiated link speed and width. A driver of ** NONE ** means the device enumerated but nothing bound to it - either the module is missing or the driver probe failed, which PCI Kernel Messages will show.
PCIDrivers.cmd: if [ ! -d /sys/bus/pci/devices ]; then echo "No PCI bus present on this system"; else for d in /sys/bus/pci/devices/*; do [ -d "$d" ] || continue; a=$(basename "$d"); drv=$(readlink -f "$d/driver" 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$drv" ]; then drv=$(basename "$drv"); else drv="** NONE **"; fi; ven=$(sed -e "s/0x//" "$d/vendor" 2>/dev/null); dev=$(sed -e "s/0x//" "$d/device" 2>/dev/null); cs=$(cat "$d/current_link_speed" 2>/dev/null); cw=$(cat "$d/current_link_width" 2>/dev/null); ms=$(cat "$d/max_link_speed" 2>/dev/null); mw=$(cat "$d/max_link_width" 2>/dev/null); echo "$a  [$ven:$dev]  class $(cat "$d/class" 2>/dev/null)"; echo "    driver : $drv"; echo "    link   : ${cs:-n/a} x${cw:-?}   (max ${ms:-n/a} x${mw:-?})"; done; fi

PCIKernelMessages.title: PCI Kernel Messages
PCIKernelMessages.description: Kernel messages from the PCI subsystem and from any driver bound to a PCI address - link training, BAR assignment, ASPM/AER, and driver probe failures. Capped at the last 300 matching lines.
PCIKernelMessages.cmd: out=$(dmesg 2>/dev/null | grep -E "([0-9a-f]{4}:[0-9a-f]{2}:[0-9a-f]{2}\.[0-9a-f])|brcm-pcie|pci_bus|pcieport|PCIe|\] PCI" | tail -n 300); if [ -n "$out" ]; then echo "$out"; else echo "No PCI-related kernel messages found"; fi

PCIDeviceDetails.title: PCI Device Details
PCIDeviceDetails.description: Full configuration space decode for every device - BARs, capabilities, link status and power management. Verbose.
PCIDeviceDetails.cmd: if [ ! -d /sys/bus/pci/devices ]; then echo "No PCI bus present on this system"; elif ! command -v lspci >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "lspci not installed (pciutils package)"; else lspci -vvnn; fi

PCIeDeviceTreeConfig.title: PCIe Device Tree Config
PCIeDeviceTreeConfig.description: Configured state of each PCIe controller as the firmware handed it to the kernel: whether the slot is enabled, its maximum link speed, and the dma-ranges window that decides which addresses a device is allowed to DMA to. Useful when a device enumerates but its driver fails to allocate DMA memory.
PCIeDeviceTreeConfig.cmd: found=0; for n in /proc/device-tree/*/pcie@* /proc/device-tree/*/*/pcie@*; do [ -d "$n" ] || continue; found=1; echo "=== $n"; echo "    status         : $(tr -d "\000" < "$n/status" 2>/dev/null)"; if command -v dtc >/dev/null 2>&1; then dtc -f -I fs -O dts "$n" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "max-link-speed|dma-ranges|linux,pci-domain" | sed -e "s/^	*/    /"; fi; echo; done; [ "$found" = "1" ] || echo "No PCIe nodes found in the device tree"

MediaChecks.grpDescription: Pass / fail checks across the PipeWire, WirePlumber and GStreamer media stack. Each check answers a question rather than printing state: every line is marked [PASS], [WARN], [FAIL], [INFO] or [SKIP], and every failure says what breaks and what to do about it. Start here, then use the Media Backend tab for the raw output behind an answer.

PWCheckServices.title: Service & Runtime Health
PWCheckServices.description: Are the PipeWire, WirePlumber and PipeWire-Pulse services up, reachable and stable? Catches crash loops, missing sockets, lost realtime priority and recent service errors.

PWCheckConfig.title: Configuration Integrity
PWCheckConfig.description: Is the deployed PipeWire configuration complete, parseable and the same as what the web pages last saved? Catches unapplied changes, corrupt JSON, syntax errors that make PipeWire silently drop a whole file, sample rate mismatches, and settings pointing at sinks that no longer exist.

PWCheckGraph.title: Graph vs Configuration
PWCheckGraph.description: Does the running audio graph match what the configuration asks for? Compares every node FPP declares and every link target it names against the nodes PipeWire actually created, so a group that exists on screen but not in the graph is named outright.

PWCheckAlsa.title: ALSA Hardware & Contention
PWCheckAlsa.description: Are the sound cards the audio groups reference actually present, unmuted, and not held by another process? Also checks that no group asks a card for more channels than it has.

PWCheckGStreamer.title: GStreamer Elements & Plugins
PWCheckGStreamer.description: Are all the GStreamer elements FPP uses installed, and do the PipeWire plugin and daemon come from the same release? A mismatched pipewiresink plays every playlist silently with nothing logged, so it is checked explicitly.

PWCheckNetwork.title: Network Audio & Video Outputs
PWCheckNetwork.description: AES67, Opus RTP and RTSP output health: whether streams are fed by an output group, whether PTP is running, whether the bound interfaces exist, and whether the RTSP port is actually listening.

PWCheckVideo.title: Video Input & Output
PWCheckVideo.description: Do the configured video input sources point at capture devices that exist, and do the video output consumers point at displays that are plugged in and sources that are still configured?

PWCheckPerformance.title: Latency, Clocking & Dropouts
PWCheckPerformance.description: Graph quantum and sample rate, xrun (dropout) counts, CPU load, and Raspberry Pi under-voltage or thermal throttling - the usual causes of crackling that is not a configuration fault.

PWCheckSmoke.title: End-to-end Pipeline Test
PWCheckSmoke.description: Runs real GStreamer pipelines at zero volume to prove the paths FPP uses can actually be built: playback to the default sink, playback to the configured sink, and capture from PipeWire. Also lists which audio formats have a decoder. Makes no sound.

DevTools.grpDescription: Tools for building and developing FPP on this device

NOCCHelpers.title: Available NOCC Helpers
NOCCHelpers.description: The distributed-compile (nocc) helpers this device can see on the network, from nocc-daemon -print-discovered-servers, with the IP address, port and host name of each
NOCCHelpers.cmd: command -v nocc-daemon >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "nocc-daemon is not installed"; exit 0; }; out=$(nocc-daemon -print-discovered-servers 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "No NOCC helpers discovered"; exit 0; }; printf "%-16s %-7s %s\n" IP PORT HOSTNAME; echo "$out" | while read s; do h=${s%:*}; p=${s##*:}; case "$h" in *[a-zA-Z]*) name=$h; ip=$(getent ahostsv4 "$h" | head -1 | cut -d" " -f1);; *) ip=$h; name=$(timeout 3 avahi-resolve -a "$h" 2>/dev/null | cut -f2); [ -n "$name" ] || name=$(getent hosts "$h" | tr -s " " | cut -d" " -f2 | head -1);; esac; printf "%-16s %-7s %s\n" "${ip:--}" "$p" "${name:--}"; done
NOCCHelpers.manualCrashReportCmd: command -v nocc-daemon >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "nocc-daemon is not installed"; exit 0; }; echo "NOCC helpers discovered: $(nocc-daemon -print-discovered-servers 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"

DevSettings.title: Developer Settings
DevSettings.description: The Developer tab settings that decide where FPP updates come from and how it is built. The GitHub access token is never shown: **** means one is set, blank means none
DevSettings.cmd: f=/home/fpp/media/settings; get() { grep -i "^$1 = " $f 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed -e "s/^[^=]*= *//" -e "s/\"//g"; }; row() { printf "%-30s  %s\n" "$1" "$2"; }; row Setting Value; row "------------------------------" "--------------------"; v=$(get gitRemote); row "Git Remote Repository" "${v:-origin (default)}"; v=$(get gitHubUser); row "GitHub User Name" "${v:-none}"; if [ -n "$(get gitHubPAT)" ]; then pat="****"; else pat="none"; fi; row "GitHub Personal Access Token" "$pat"; v=$(get DistributedCompile); row "Distributed Compile" "${v:-off (default)}"
DevSettings.manualCrashReportCmd: f=/home/fpp/media/settings; get() { grep -i "^$1 = " $f 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed -e "s/^[^=]*= *//" -e "s/\"//g"; }; row() { printf "%-30s  %s\n" "$1" "$2"; }; row Setting Value; row "------------------------------" "--------------------"; v=$(get gitRemote); row "Git Remote Repository" "${v:-origin (default)}"; if [ -n "$(get gitHubPAT)" ]; then pat="****"; else pat="none"; fi; row "GitHub Personal Access Token" "$pat"; v=$(get DistributedCompile); row "Distributed Compile" "${v:-off (default)}"

PMICVOLTAGE.title: RPI Power Supply
PMICVOLTAGE.description: Raspberry Pi power telemetry (Pi 5 and later), parsed for readability: measured 5V input-rail voltage (EXT5V_V), core voltage/current and estimated PMIC power, the USB-C PD negotiated supply-current limit, decoded throttle/under-voltage flags (including since-boot), SoC temperature, and the RTC backup-cell voltage. Readings not available on the board are reported as such. Expected nominal input is 5.0V (5.1V with the official PSU); the firmware under-voltage trip is around 4.63-4.85V.
PMICVOLTAGE.cmd:
P=$(vcgencmd pmic_read_adc 2>/dev/null); if printf "%s" "$P" | grep -q EXT5V_V; then EV=$(printf "%s" "$P" | sed -n "s/.*EXT5V_V[^=]*=//p"); EV=${EV%V}; printf "Input voltage (EXT5V_V): %.2f V
" "$EV"; CV=$(printf "%s" "$P" | sed -n "s/.*VDD_CORE_V[^=]*=//p"); CV=${CV%V}; printf "Core voltage (VDD_CORE): %.2f V
" "$CV"; CA=$(printf "%s" "$P" | sed -n "s/.*VDD_CORE_A[^=]*=//p"); CA=${CA%A}; printf "Core current (VDD_CORE): %.2f A
" "$CA"; PW=$(printf "%s" "$P" | awk -F= "{ n=\$1; gsub(/^ +| +[a-z].*/,"",n); if (n ~ /_V$/) v[substr(n,1,length(n)-2)]=\$2+0; else if (n ~ /_A$/) c[substr(n,1,length(n)-2)]=\$2+0 } END { t=0; for(k in c) if(k in v) t+=c[k]*v[k]; printf "%.2f", t }"); echo "Estimated PMIC power: $PW W"; else echo "Input voltage (EXT5V_V): not available on this Raspberry Pi model"; fi; if [ -r /sys/firmware/devicetree/base/chosen/power/max_current ]; then M=$(od --endian=big -An -i /sys/firmware/devicetree/base/chosen/power/max_current | tr -d " "); printf "Negotiated supply current: %d.%01d A
" "$((M/1000))" "$(((M%1000)/100))"; else echo "Negotiated supply current: not available on this Raspberry Pi model"; fi; T=$(vcgencmd get_throttled 2>/dev/null | sed -n "s/throttled=//p"); T=${T:-0x0}; S=""; [ $((T & 0x1)) -ne 0 ] && S="$S under-voltage"; [ $((T & 0x2)) -ne 0 ] && S="$S freq-capped"; [ $((T & 0x4)) -ne 0 ] && S="$S throttled"; [ $((T & 0x8)) -ne 0 ] && S="$S soft-temp-limit"; [ $((T & 0x10000)) -ne 0 ] && S="$S under-voltage-since-boot"; [ $((T & 0x20000)) -ne 0 ] && S="$S freq-capped-since-boot"; [ $((T & 0x40000)) -ne 0 ] && S="$S throttled-since-boot"; [ $((T & 0x80000)) -ne 0 ] && S="$S soft-temp-limit-since-boot"; [ -z "$S" ] && S=" none"; echo "Throttle/under-voltage ($T):$S"; TP=$(vcgencmd measure_temp 2>/dev/null | sed -n "s/.*temp=//;s/.C$//p"); [ -n "$TP" ] && printf "SoC temperature: %s C
" "$TP"; RB=""; for d in /sys/class/rtc/rtc*; do case "$(cat "$d/name" 2>/dev/null)" in *rpi_rtc*) RB="$d/battery_voltage";; esac; done; if [ -n "$RB" ]; then B=$(cat "$RB" 2>/dev/null); if [ "${B:-0}" -ge 1000000 ] 2>/dev/null; then printf "RTC battery: %d.%02d V
" "$((B/1000000))" "$(((B%1000000)/10000))"; else echo "RTC battery: not fitted"; fi; else echo "RTC battery: not available (Pi 5 RTC disabled or not present)"; fi
